preamble: Depalatalization (hardening) of the palatalized alveolar nasal [nʲ] to plain [n]. In Slavic, consonants softened before front vowels in Common Slavic and Old East Slavic; Ukrainian later hardened them before /e/ (Russian keeps the soft consonant), and West Slavic Czech depalatalized consonants before e and ä in its early history.

examples.note: Old East Slavic softened /n/ before /e/ (9th c. /ˈnɛbɔ/ > 11th c. /ˈnʲɛbɔ/); Ukrainian hardened it again, whereas Russian keeps [ˈnʲebə].
Same hardening of the nasal before original *e.

examples.from: Proto-Slavic *nebo 'sky' (cf. Polish niebo [ˈɲɛbɔ] with preserved softness)
examples.note: Early Czech depalatalized consonants before e and ä, unlike Polish, which kept and strengthened the softness.
